title: EXP-138 — FX_LoginPortal: Hashed FX_LoginUsers Lookup in FX_ProcessLogin
objective: Replace the C# Form Script of the existing User-scoped Form FX_LoginPortal (EXP-133) with the committed source assets/FX_Login/FX_LoginPortal.cs.txt (SHA-256 0ba26a44b67afee8a8b38dc5502dff1eecfe330bc809e7118ba52cc526b2514b, supplied by the operator) so that FX_ProcessLogin(string username, string password) loads FX_LoginUsers filtered on FX_Username, compares the SHA-256 hex of the supplied password with the stored FX_PasswordHash, and sets the existing Global variable FX_vLoginResult to exactly one of missing, empty, unknown, invalid, ok or error. Install it by the accepted EXP-136 T15 full-content fill route, perform one ordinary Designer Save, verify persistence through a Designer reopen, then prove at runtime through the unchanged FX_Login Web User Control that fx_probe with the fake test value fx-probe-only returns ok, fx_probe with fx-wrong-value returns invalid, and fx_nobody with fx-probe-only returns unknown. The ok result also proves end to end that the EXP-137 record stored fx_probe in FX_Username and the hash in FX_PasswordHash.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, the EXP-133, EXP-136 and EXP-137 records (especially EXP-133 T7, EXP-136 T15 to T23 and the EXP-137 acceptance), the committed source assets/FX_Login/FX_LoginPortal.cs.txt and recipes/session/session-expiry-and-stale-designer.md before browser mutation.
Set worker_tool_policy.deny_browser_javascript to true before any browser operation.
Before every screenshot or input, select the intended browser tab (browser tabs select) so it is the foreground tab; screenshots of a background tab time out (EXP-137 T6 and T7).

Read-only preflight: verify the account header identifies anton.ramos@3mworks.com.ph, the configuration is G6R8LJ9Q4E8C2Z8Y_MONGOOSE_DEM_DEFAULT, Designer editing scope is User, and FX_LoginPortal opens in the Designer as the User version with Script Language Visual C#.

Read-only readback of the current FX_LoginPortal Form Script (open the Form Script editor, read, then Cancel) and comparison with the EXP-133 T7 committed method; record any difference and stop on an unexpected script.

Install the committed source exactly once by the EXP-136 T15 route: open the Form Script editor, click inside the editor, Ctrl+A, one full-content fill with the complete text of assets/FX_Login/FX_LoginPortal.cs.txt, read back the whole script before OK, then OK.
Reopen the Form Script editor read-only after OK, read back the whole script, record the Compile Result Output and Errors exactly as observed, then Cancel.
Perform exactly one ordinary Designer Save of FX_LoginPortal and capture the response and the clean post-Save state.
Verify persistence by closing FX_LoginPortal in the Designer and reopening it (or a supported Designer reload as in EXP-134 T5), then read back the Form Script once more.

Open FX_LoginPortal at runtime in the Web Client, using the EXP-135 T9 portal-reload route once when the Web Client needs to load the saved script (top-level navigation to the portal URL, then Mongoose from the portal navigation search).

Run exactly three runtime Sign In attempts with fake fixture values only, each followed by a screenshot of the displayed result text: fx_probe with fx-probe-only (expected ok); fx_probe with fx-wrong-value (expected invalid); fx_nobody with fx-probe-only (expected unknown).

If the Web User Control frame exposes no accessibility reference, a native coordinate click on a control verified from a fresh screenshot is permitted as the AGENTS.md last resort and must be recorded (EXP-136 T23).
Write the experiment record and bounded evidence under evidence/EXP-138/, record every changed object, and reconcile all actions in a final audit.

acceptance_checks.description: Pre-mutation evidence identifies the account anton.ramos@3mworks.com.ph, configuration G6R8LJ9Q4E8C2Z8Y_MONGOOSE_DEM_DEFAULT, Designer User scope and FX_LoginPortal loaded as the User version with Script Language Visual C#.
The pre-change Form Script is read back and compared with the EXP-133 T7 method (FX_ProcessLogin returning missing, empty or received); any difference is recorded before mutation.

Exactly one full-content fill installs the committed source (operator-supplied SHA-256 0ba26a44b67afee8a8b38dc5502dff1eecfe330bc809e7118ba52cc526b2514b). The readback before OK and the read-only readback after OK both show class FX_LoginPortal, the usings System.Security.Cryptography and System.Text, the signature public string FX_ProcessLogin(string username, string password), the IDOClient.LoadCollection call on FX_LoginUsers with properties FX_Username, FX_PasswordHash, the six result codes, the assignment to ThisForm.Variables(FX_vLoginResult) and the private FX_Sha256Hex helper, with no leftover EXP-133 method. The Compile Result is recorded exactly as observed.
Exactly one ordinary Designer Save of FX_LoginPortal; the response and clean post-Save state (Save disabled) are captured.
After a Designer close and reopen (or supported reload), the Form Script read back from FX_LoginPortal still matches AC-3.

FX_LoginPortal opens at runtime in the Web Client with the FX_Login username field, password field and Sign In button visible, after the portal-reload route when needed, with the account context re-established.
Sign In with username fx_probe and the fake test value fx-probe-only displays the result text ok.
Sign In with username fx_probe and fx-wrong-value displays the result text invalid.
Sign In with username fx_nobody and fx-probe-only displays the result text unknown.
Only result codes are displayed; no password or fixture value is stored or shown outside the typed input boxes. FX_LoginUsers, the FX_Login assets and the FX_vLoginResult definition are not edited.

The final audit reconciles every Form Script fill, OK, Cancel, Designer Save, close, reopen, portal reload and Sign In attempt, lists all changed objects (only the FX_LoginPortal Form Script), and records the evidence-file inventory and confinement.

initial_instruction: EXP-138 T1 — PREFLIGHT ONLY. Before using the browser, set worker_tool_policy.deny_browser_javascript=true. Read AGENTS.md, the EXP-133, EXP-136 and EXP-137 records, the committed source assets/FX_Login/FX_LoginPortal.cs.txt and the session-recovery recipe. Select the intended browser tab before each screenshot or input. Using supported rendered Mongoose surfaces, capture the account identity, configuration and Designer User scope; open FX_LoginPortal in the Designer and confirm it is the User version with Script Language Visual C#; open the Form Script editor, read back the current script, compare it with the EXP-133 T7 method, then Cancel. Record findings in evidence/EXP-138/ with a concise gate summary. Do not fill the editor, press OK, Save, run a Sign In attempt or change any Mongoose object in T1. notes: Written by the operator assistant because the coordinator proposal step failed three times on a ChatGPT composer fill timeout; modelled on the approved EXP-137 brief. Rationale: EXP-133 proved the FX_LoginPortal bridge (received); EXP-137 created FX_LoginUsers with the fake fx_probe row and its SHA-256 hash. This experiment completes the FX_ reproduction of the Mock login (EXP-130 T5 sections 2, 4, 5 and 7.1) with a hashed comparison and nonsensitive result codes. The C# source was compiled and unit-tested locally against stubbed Mongoose types before commit (commit 09486c8).
